title: Traffic credit accounting and preemptive eviction protocol for region failover
creator: Priya Patel
description: We need a deterministic accounting model and operational protocol that lets regions borrow/repay SLO capacity (traffic credits) during multi-region failover, and a preemptive eviction algorithm that uses that accounting to make fair, low-friction decisions under capacity pressure. This ticket defines SLI bindings, ledger semantics, transfer APIs, circuit-breaker integration points, and an operator-facing runbook for contested capacity events.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical traffic-credit ledger design documented and approved by SRE and Product
API surface for credit transfers (deposit, withdraw, escrow, reconcile) implemented and covered by unit tests
Controller enforces preemptive eviction policy deterministically for top-10 tenants in a simulated regional failover (integration test)
Dashboards displaying credits, burn-rates, pending transfers, and per-tenant eviction score are available in Console
Playbook verified by a chaos run that simulates regional ejection with >90% success of graceful failover paths
design_notes: Goals: avoid surprise wholesale throttles, enable predictable tenant-level fairness, and permit short-term credit borrowing with automated repayment. Tradeoffs: strong consistency for ledger operations increases latency and operational complexity; eventual consistency allows higher throughput but requires reconciliation and compensating actions. We lean toward strongly consistent transfers for credit escrow and borrow operations during failover windows; normal replenishment can be eventual. See section on 'Atomic vs. Eventually-Consistent Transfers' for rationale.
implementation_plan: 1) Add traffic_credit SLI dimensions: success_rate (>=99.5%), p95_latency_ms (<200ms), quality_regression_rate (<1% triggered by eval harness). 2) Implement ledger service (new table traffic_credits{tenant,region,available,escrowed,borrowed,last_replenish_ts}) with transactional transfer endpoints. 3) Integrate with circuit-breaker: when region enters degraded state, controller attempts to borrow credits from peer regions using transfer API; on failure escalate to preemptive eviction. 4) Eviction scoring: score = alpha*burn_rate + beta*(1 - credit_ratio) + gamma*sla_priority; configurable weights. 5) Expose metrics and Console panels, wire alerts to PagerDuty and Console incident view. 6) Add integration tests and a chaos runbook.

notes: Eviction policy must be deterministic across controller replicas to avoid split decisions; tie-breaker is tenant id hash with region priority bias.
Buckets: short-term burst credits (10s-2m), medium escrow (2m-30m), long-term allocation (>=30m). Borrowing allowed only from short/medium during emergency windows.
Operators should prefer borrow->graceful-degrade->hard-evict ordering. Hard-evict only when credits exhausted and circuit-breaker thresholds exceeded twice within 5 minutes.
